findings.expected: One stated outcome for a C misread on each accepted proof route (product, divided, log-absolute, explicit-root), or the fixture explicitly limited to the product route.
findings.actual: The fixture says "Since the constant differentiates to zero, a complete proof still establishes the actual target canonically: 9/9" without naming a route. That is true on the product route only: there C enters just S3 (zero constant derivative). On the mapped divided route (WO:112-114; exemplar:133 shows C as 4/y, -4y'/y^2 and the back-substitution 4=3e^{2x}y+y^2) the C=5 learner writes 3e^{2x}+y=5/y, gets y'=-6e^{2x}y^2/(y^2+5) (canonical y^2+4) and back-substitutes the false 5=3e^{2x}y+y^2 to reach the target.
findings.evidence: Own sympy: divided intermediate differs from canonical; after back-substitution it equals the target. Under canonical marking of this ineligible datum S3 ("correctly differentiate its remaining implicit y-terms") and S4 ("S1-S3 all correct") fail: 7/9. Read as "correct derivative of their term", it is 9/9. On the explicit-root route the C=5 root carries sqrt(9e^{4x}+20) against canonical +16, giving as little as 6/9. Product route: 9/9. The same misread therefore costs 0, 2 or 3 marks by route. Eligible treatment would give a route-independent 8/9. That is an owner option, not a defect.
findings.repair: Qualify the 9/9 fixture as the product route. Add an E/F fixture stating whether S1-S4 on the divided, log and explicit-root routes are judged against canonical C when a C misread is ineligible.

findings.locator: work-orders/WB8227-implicit-normal.md:142 ("It cannot become a fresh eligible misread in a later part") vs :153 ("This fresh datum is first used in (b)")
findings.expected: The datum identity used by the once-only ledger is defined, so an ineligible misread cannot re-enter as a new eligible datum.
findings.actual: The later first-use fixture treats a printed coefficient of the displayed derivative as a datum separate from the curve parameters. Take canonical (3,2,-4) with a=3 read as 4 in (a), which is ineligible (S1,S3 = 2/4). In (b) the learner applies the displayed formula and reads its denominator 3e^{2x} as 4e^{2x}. This gives m=24/(4-8)=-6, m_perp=1/6 and y+4=x/6.
findings.evidence: As a fresh datum this passes all four WO:142 conditions: the curve is not misread, P is on the curve, m=-6 is finite and nonzero, the chain is present and the supplied target represents the curve. It is then eligible, scoring 2/4+2/2+3/3-1 = 6/9. As the same datum as a it is canonical, scoring 2/4+1/2+2/3 = 5/9. This is the calc-D3-02(ii) 5/9 versus 6/9 split, reached through a different response.
findings.repair: E/F: define datum identity. For example, a displayed-formula number that restates an already-ruled curve parameter inherits that ruling. Add this as a fixture.

findings.locator: subject-rules.md:67 and shared-misread-policy.json operational_rules ("first earned A/B on that datum"); stationary WO:118,:120,:122; exemplar:125,:127,:131
findings.expected: The deduction-candidate rule names its unit.
findings.actual: Every stationary deduction falls on a criterion whose value does not depend on the misread constant: P2 (derivative), I1 (derivative) and C2 (types). WO:120 says "earliest earned A/B slot of this first-use part". The oracle tags every criterion of every using part with the datum. "A/B on that datum" therefore means "any A/B in a part that uses the datum".
findings.evidence: A criterion-level implementation (only A/B whose value uses c) would deduct nothing in the WO:122 fixture, giving 4/6 instead of 3/6 and restoring the D3-S02(a) free misread. It would also give 4/6 instead of 3/6 in the built I4 case. The current WO text read as a whole is consistent with the part-level reading, and each stated fixture has one outcome.
findings.repair: When next touched, add "(any A/B in a part that uses that datum)" to MR03-OPS or the stationary WO line :116.

findings.locator: review/opus-5-5-d3-confirm/findings.md §D Notes calc-D3-01 (our text); work-orders/WB8227-implicit-normal.md:142 last sentence
findings.expected: An accurate record of which implicit misreads the point-on-curve guard excludes.
findings.actual: Our D3 note said the guard makes a, C and q misreads ineligible. For q this is inaccurate. Reading q as the other y-intercept, -a-q, keeps P on the curve in 27/27 tuples. On 4 curves both intercepts are admitted negative points: (3,k,-1) with (3,k,-2), and (4,k,-1) with (4,k,-3). Such a misread passes the D4 conditions and is eligible.
findings.evidence: Own survey over q' in -9..9: 27 on-curve, 459 off. a misreads: 0 of 216 on-curve. C misreads: 0 of 1620. k misreads: all on-curve. WO:142 ends "For a point misread in the normal part ... N3 still needs the canonical line" without separating an on-curve (eligible) point from an off-curve one. In practice N3 is 0 under either reading for the usual response, because the learner keeps the gradient from the true P.
findings.repair: None required for approval. Correct our own record. In E/F, state whether an on-curve point misread in (c) receives N3 follow-through.
